name: CI / Zenoh backend

permissions: read-all

jobs:

  build-zenoh:
    name: build & test (zenoh feature)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy

      # The Zenoh backend is built with the DDS default turned off.
      - name: check (zenoh)
        run: cargo check --no-default-features --features zenoh

      - name: clippy (zenoh)
        run: cargo clippy --no-default-features --features zenoh --lib --bins -- -D warnings

      # The zenoh-backend example must compile (and lint clean). The DDS
      # examples are gated on the `dds` feature (Cargo.toml `required-features`)
      # and are skipped under this feature set.
      - name: clippy examples (zenoh)
        run: cargo clippy --no-default-features --features zenoh --examples -- -D warnings

      # `--lib` only: the crate-level doctest exercises the DDS API and is not
      # meant to compile under the zenoh backend. Serial to keep session ports
      # from contending.
      - name: test (zenoh, lib)
        run: cargo test --no-default-features --features zenoh --lib -- --test-threads=1

      # The DDS backend must also build when selected explicitly with default
      # features off.
      - name: check (dds, explicit)
        run: cargo check --no-default-features --features dds

      # Both backends may be enabled in the same build (ADR-0010 Phase 5):
      # entity types are namespaced under `ros2_client::dds` /
      # `ros2_client::zenoh`, so there is no more feature exclusivity to
      # enforce. `--lib` only: examples/tests are written against a single
      # backend's crate-root re-exports and are not meant to compile dual.
      - name: check (dds + zenoh, lib)
        run: cargo check --features dds,zenoh --lib

      - name: clippy (dds + zenoh, lib)
        run: cargo clippy --features dds,zenoh --lib -- -D warnings

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
